You saw a robin this morning. You wrote it down. By tonight, that note could say anything — and nobody would know.
Vickrey is a field journal that seals what you saw: a signed record anyone can check later.
Take a photo. An open model — Gemma, running on a server for this demo — looks for about twenty seconds, and suggests: Robin.
But a model only suggests. You decide. Confirm it, or correct it — and your decision is sealed into the record.
The record is signed on the device and chained to the one before it.
Now, change it. Edit the copy waiting to sync, and the seal cracks. Sync refuses to send it. Your journal still holds what you sealed.
Put it back, and sync. The ledger — a mock in this demo — checks the seal. Verified. Only a hash, a coarse area and the species leave the device. Never the photo.
Nature data is a shared effort. GBIF reports more than three billion occurrence records, from around twenty-three hundred institutions. Records you can check are worth having.
Vickrey is open source, and early. Next: models on the phone, a public ledger, and a proper walk outside.
